nodes.description: A heterozygous germline loss-of-function variant in KCNQ1 reduces the function of the Kv7.1 channel, the alpha subunit of the IKs channel complex. Two broad mechanisms are recognized. Truncating, frameshift, and splice variants are generally modelled as haploinsufficient, with at most about half the channel function lost. Missense variants and in-frame deletions are generally modelled as dominant negative, where the mutant subunit co-assembles with and impairs wild-type subunits, for example by a trafficking defect. Variant class and location (pore, transmembrane, C-terminal) modify arrhythmic risk.

nodes.description: When sympathetic tone and heart rate rise, the normal response is a larger, faster-activating IKs that shortens the ventricular action potential. With reduced IKs the action potential and QT interval fail to shorten, which is why LQT1 events cluster during exertion and why the QT response to exercise is diagnostically informative.
